utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty, I understand you have some matters to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Just one matter, Your Honour, and it will be brief. On the 22nd of June, the Prosecution was notified of the Defence's intent to soon call Witness T-22. The Prosecution yesterday, the 25th of June, made a motion to exclude that testimony on the grounds of relevancy. It was filed yesterday afternoon. The Defence, of course, has under the Rules 14 days in which to respond, but I'm wondering if as a matter of courtesy, more to the witness than to the Prosecution, it might be possible to request a response sooner than that, perhaps even as soon as the day after tomorrow, the 28th, even if it is oral, since if the Chamber rules for the Prosecution on this motion that would allow it to be decided before the witness leaves the region and has the expense and inconvenience of travelling to the Netherlands. That's all I wanted to say before the witness came in. Thank you, Your Honour. [Trial Chamber confers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty, you would have received the Defence 65 ter list of witnesses and exhibits long ago, so why are you now at this late stage making this submission?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: We were notified on the Friday, Your Honour, of the witness's full name, date of birth, and of the Defence's intent to offer his testimony on the 3rd of July, and we made the motion on the Monday. The full name and date of birth are quite important in identifying these witnesses and understanding their testimony when we do our document searches --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You mean there was no name at all?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: There was not a full name, nor was there a date of birth, and distinguishing by date of birth is very important because of the limited number of family names that we work with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But presumably the motion that you have made, its substance would not depend on the name. It's the -- the motion that you are making is based on the -- the summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: The motion that we are making is based upon the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: However, the motion can change or relevancy could have been revealed when we were in a position to understand the witness's testimony by knowing who the witness was. A witness might well live a long way from Sarajevo, for example, and that might be in the 65 ter summary, but then when we specifically and uniquely identify that person, perhaps it turns out to be someone who's quite central to events inside Sarajevo. And I just have to say that this is a continuing issue with the 65 ter summaries. A couple of witnesses from now a witness will be called -- we have two separate people that we are looking at and finding documents on because we don't have a father's name or a date of birth. And so this is a continuing issue, and as I say upon being able to uniquely identify the witness, which was last Friday, we brought the motion on the Monday. And yes, it is based on the 65 ter summary, and if that's going to be fatal to our submission, that's the way it's going to go, but that is the explanation and the response to your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So we can expect more motions of this kind?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Unless we -- unless we start getting 65 ter summaries that contain a father's name and a date of birth so that we can uniquely identify the witnesses that are being called, I cannot rule out additional motions being brought. We will do our best. I certainly take the Chamber's point. We will go through the 65 ter summaries. We will try and make any such motions based on the summaries, but even then they could change or be withdrawn, for example, at the last moment when we figure out who the person really is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, do you have anything to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, briefly. During the Prosecution case and having in mind the summaries we received from them, in a number of cases all they provided was just the pseudonym, not even the first or the last name. We tried in each and every case to provide them with a first and last name. There's not a single witness that wasn't identified in that way and we did this immediately at the same time as when we did the submission of the 65 ters -- 65 ter summaries. We are not bound by the Rules to provide the name of the father, date of birth, or any other --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We -- the Chamber will have to come to a decision on this matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's Mr. Tapuskovic, I believe, to conclude.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I thought that I had a little bit of cross-examination left to go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Oh, you still have some?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I -- we wrapped up. I had finished one topic and rather than continue to the next one, we stopped for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I recall. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If we could please see the photograph which we ended with yesterday, which I believe is Prosecution Exhibit 786.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. -- sorry. I mispronounced your name. Mr. Visnjic, on the screen in front of you, you see the photograph that we ended with yesterday. And could you tell us again what's the name of the building that has the X on the right-hand side as you look at it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This building that I marked, I don't think it is the building you designated as being the building of Energoinvest, that's not the building. However, there was a Unioninvest building, and if this is the Vrbanja bridge, then it should be the Unioninvest building where the OHR offices are nowadays. If this is so, I might be able to point out the building where the Invest Bank building was which was entered by the terrorist group and they eventually managed to reach the third floor, although I don't see here the Vrbanja bridge or the Unioninvest or the OHR building. I also cannot see the former Assembly building. I do see the land historical museum and some other buildings which are across from the museum, closer to us. Could you please show me a photograph with the Unioninvest building?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Well, what we're trying to do, sir, is identify the building. Is the building that the ABiH troops entered, where they got to the third floor, is that on the photograph that is in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think these are the so-called Metalka buildings. There was number 1 and number 2, but I'm not sure whether that's the building that I had thought it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did some thinking overnight. Yesterday I wanted to ask you to show me the Unioninvest building or the Vrbanja bridge, and if I were able to see that on the photograph I would be able to tell you exactly which building that is. Otherwise, I cannot be sure. I think this is the Metalka building, but this is not the building that we are looking for. It should be somewhere to the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. Thank you. We -- if these are the Metalka buildings, number 1 and 2, can you just tell us where the building that you were talking about, the building where the enemy soldiers entered and got to the third floor, where it would be in relation to what we do see only the screen in front of us. Would we go to the right? Would we go to the left? Where would they be?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it should be to the right. Can you show me the Unioninvest building and the Vrbanja bridge? If you are able to do that, I can tell you exactly which building that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: They are not on this photograph which is the one that's loaded into the computer, so we can't show that to you right now, but there might be a photograph that we will see in a couple of minutes that will help you with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: For now let's take this off and let's put up Defence Exhibit 272 --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Which is the combat report from the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina about the attack on that building that you talked about yesterday. Now, yesterday you looked at this while Mr. Tapuskovic was asking you questions, and we see here that the date on this report is 21st of July, 1995. Am I correct about the date?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that the date here is the 21st of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And in paragraph number 2 it says: "The action was carried out against the Chetnik bunker in Ivesta Bank, third floor, in which Chetniks," and then I can't read it, "were permanently stationed." Have I read that properly?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you have.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: So what this report is talking about is an attack by the ABiH on the 21st of July against a position of your army in the Invest Bank building. Is that a fair summary of what the subject of this report is?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's precisely what happened. Their sabotage group attacked the building in which our soldiers were. They attacked one of its wings. They took control of it and proceeded onwards to the third floor, where I believe they killed two elderly people. While carrying out that attack, they had significant fire support from the rear --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Sir, I just need to stop you right there --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: -- I know you've got a lot to say about this and it's an important subject to you, but I'm just asking for now about things that are in the document. So there were soldiers of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps in this building on the 21st of July, correct, those are the troops who were defending; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And the building had been held by the SRK before the 21st of July; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the area of responsibility of my battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And this attack, although there were losses suffered, this attack was repulsed. The Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not hold this building, did they? They were driven out?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And this is -- and this building was then held by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps until the end of the war, until Dayton; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: This building is a tall building, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Maybe some six floors, while the Unioninvest building was far taller. It was under the control of the A B&H as of the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the building that is concerned in this report, the Invest Banka building, this building is along the Miljacka river, is it not? Along the south bank--

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: -- in an area controlled by the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps during the war; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And lastly, if we could please see Prosecution Exhibit 201. For the record, this is not on the Prosecution's spreadsheet. I did speak with Defence counsel about this this morning, and there was no objection interposed to my using this photograph with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Sir, I'll ask you to just take a look at this photograph. As with previous photographs I'll ask you to just get your bearings, figure out what's where. There is an X on one building, it was made by an earlier witness; you don't need to worry about that. But just take a moment. When you're ready to proceed, when you're oriented, just let me know.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- well, the high-rises here, it's Unioninvest and Vaso Miskin factory with this smoke-stack as far as I can see. To the left is Energoinvest building, its administrative building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Let's just hold on right there. Yesterday you testified about a sniper team going into the so-called shopping buildings. Do you remember telling me about that when I was asking you some questions?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do the shopping buildings appear on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: With the usher's assistance, would you please draw a blue circle around the shopping buildings. It will just be a moment, sir. This technology usually works very well, but sometimes there are problems. Okay. Let's try this again. Okay. Can you take a -- do you see that photograph that's now -- it's to your right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If there's a pen there - and if there isn't, I'll give you one - can you draw a circle around the shopping buildings, please.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, these are the two buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. And there's actually three of them, it's just that one is behind the others here, is that correct, so it's a little hard to see, but there's actually three shopping buildings; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, but I only recall these two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I remember the high-rises that burnt down; they were on our side. They were fired upon from --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- these high-rises here. The person who put the X here was wrong, I think, because the high-rises were burnt down on our side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: The person who put the X there wasn't being asked about the high-rises and so forth; it was an answer to a different question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, I'll tender this photograph the witness has marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P787, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Judge Robinson, on the photograph before me, I don't see any markings -- I don't see any markings that this witness may have made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, there are two markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That is -- it's on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. This --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Madam Usher, I'm finished with marking. Thanks very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: This sniper team that went up into the shopping building, what sort of weapons did they have?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Infantry weapons, rifles of 7.9-millimetre calibre, that's it. Of course with an -- with a sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I need to interrupt for just a moment.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that as of April --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Just let me interrupt for one moment. When you say a sight, do you mean a telescopic sight?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes -- well, I wouldn't call it telescopic in my language, but it is the same sight as used in hunting rifles, if you understand what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mount it on the barrel and its range is quite great, up to 600 metres. This squad of ours, as far as I know, was formed sometime in April 1993 but was disbanded in early October 1993. After that, I wasn't able to observe those sharpshooters in my battalion. I don't think our battalion had any left after that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. And this sight, you say it's the sort of thing used on hunting rifles, so it's mounted on the barrel and you look through it like this? You look through it, a little --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As we call it, we call it a tandzara, a shot-gun which is of 7.9-millimetre calibre. There is only one barrel as you have it with hunting rifles. Next to the trigger there is a sniper sight mounted on it --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and you observe through it. Hunters use the very same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you talked about the meeting when the decision was made. If you could explain in detail what was the target for firing at this agreement in relation to everything that you talked about so far?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At this moment I know that the commander Lieutenant-Colonel Radomir Stojanovic picked a group of 12 people, due to a fierce attack from the Pero Kosoric square and Pofalici -- no, not Pofalici, just the square, this is Hrasno, from those high-rise buildings, they are high-rise buildings and they just are a bit to the left and to the west when you look at this picture and from the Mojmilo hill so that in the Moravska street we had two snipers whose tasks was to follow the other snipers, see where they're firing from, and to try to neutralise these snipers, as well as the snipers from the Pero Kosoric or from Hrasno. This is something that I know and these high-rises were the closest possible for you to be able to see where the firing is coming from the other high-rise buildings, and so that these snipers would try to successfully neutralise those firing positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, well, let us look at document P787, this photograph that was marked just a little bit before. And can you please mark the facilities or the buildings where the snipers were of the other side who, as you said, needed to be neutralised.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot see it on this photograph --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty -- sorry, please stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise for interrupting. Usually it's not a problem to mark on the other side's exhibits because an image of the Prosecution exhibit has been saved, for example, but here we're using hard copy because of the technical issues. And so this is going to change the exhibit. I don't have a problem with that, as long as we can very clearly mark who made which markings. So if we could use a different-coloured pen or write on it as to -- if the witness could make an S by the two circles he's already drawn to mark "shopping" in the English language, then we could go ahead from there. It would help if we use a different-coloured pen. I used blue. If they could use red then we'd be fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How about blue, blue and red, blue for the Prosecutor and red for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't get the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty suggested that perhaps we might use colours to indicate the Prosecutor's markings and the Defence markings, and he suggested blue for the Prosecutor and red for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I don't have any objection to that; no problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I mark this now?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, just a moment. Please don't rush. Wait. Can you mark the buildings where these firing positions of the other side were that needed to be neutralised by these people who were given that assignment.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. It's this high-rise building, this high-rise building, and this high-rise building here. These two buildings -- these three buildings --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- this is where the firing came from, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please tender this photograph now as it is now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. I've been advised, though, that we have to consider whether this exhibit should be marked twice, and it would be better to have it marked twice. Court deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, if I may. What I propose we do is have this --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment, just one moment, Your Honours, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe there was a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you draw a line here that would delineate the positions of one side and the other side, that would separate them, based on what you know, where the Miljacka River is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the Energoinvest directorate and the Bratstvo-Jedinstvo Street that goes towards the tobacco factory, tobacco factory. Now, here to the left from Energoinvest, Hrasno should be on this side, our side, where they held positions. Now we have the Miljacka --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Since you are not able to find your way around, I would just like -- ask you one more time to go back to the basic question. Did you hear that there was any kind of assignment throughout the war? You said there was a unit in 1993 which was given an assignment to act the way you said against the firing positions of the sniper nests of the other side, and now I'm asking you if during Dragomir Milosevic's time you ever heard that there was a task existing in relation to sniper activity in relation to civilians.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR VISNJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, never -- well, this wasn't a unit, it was a squad. And I said that it was active from late March 1993 until -- well, in 1993 this section was abolished. During General Milosevic's time, there was no sniper, nor did any orders come from the general to the battalions about sniper actions, particularly not on civilian targets. In 1993 there was General Galic's strict order that it was not permissible to act and that it would be strictly punished and brought before a military tribunal if it was to be discovered that any sniper fired upon a civilian. This is something that I know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions and I'm not going to be tendering this photograph as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: -- I understand he's not going to be tendering the photograph, but that's not the way -- it's been marked now, and the original was not preserved. So I would ask that -- I will ask the registrar what's the best way to proceed in this. Maybe we can get -- when the SMART Board is working, if there's no objection, we could mark it and put it in that way. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us hear the court deputy's wise words.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. My suggestion would be to rely on the record and we have the transcript that shows what the original markings were, as well as markings that were added by Defence, and this Exhibit P787 only truly reflects the Prosecution's markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. You see why I refer to his wise words. Witness, that concludes your testimony. We thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next witness is Witness T-55, Zoran Trapara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please be seated. You may begin, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have just been informed that there is a technical problem, and that until the break nothing can be done about the markings that need to be placed on certain documents. We're talking about maps. We have been informed by the -- and I don't have the paper copies in order to be able to place them on the ELMO. So there is a technical problem preventing me from beginning with my examination-in-chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, the technicians can be called in right now to look at the problem, but they need to be at the witness's desk. So the Chamber is going to adjourn for five minutes to allow the technicians to do their work. --- Break taken at 9.45 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, please begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness. Before we begin I would like to ask you to pay attention to what we are saying and to begin answering my question only after the cursor stops moving. As you can see, only when the cursor stops, then you can begin to answer my question. Can you please tell your first and last name to the Judges, please.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: I'm Zoran Trapara.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were born on the 7th of November, 1968. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In Sarajevo, in the Centar municipality?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You completed elementary and secondary technical engineering school in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You worked at the Famos factory in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And this was until the spring of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Judges where you lived while you were working.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: I lived in Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: How far was that from the Famos factory?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: It's some 2 to 300 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And when the conflict began, did you change your place of residence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I went to my family house in Donji Kotorac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I received a document from the Prosecution. I don't know if there's a translation. This is document DD004065.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know if there is a translation. We tried to see if there was one. I just have one question in relation to this document. It's still not entered into the e-court system. We did everything that we were supposed to do, but it's still not in the e-court system. There is one thing that I wanted to show the witness. Perhaps we could use the ELMO in order to do that and to put this question to this witness, if you permit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, just noting, I don't know what the document is and DD004065 was not on the list of exhibits for this witness that I received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why wasn't it on the list, Mr. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's true that -- in view of the fact -- when we actually received the document, we put it on the list additionally, but we did inform the Prosecution and we received the document from them in any event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That seems to be a standard reply. What I would say, Ms. Edgerton, is that when you see the document, if you find that you are in any way embarrassed by the lateness in the notice, then you can bring it to the Court's attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And may I just add that the Court also avails itself of the information provided by both parties to familiarise itself with the documents prior to the examination of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will not use this document in order to avoid wasting time. I just have one question, if I can put it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever fire at your own people? I'm asking you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: It's not there on the screen. I don't see it. All right. All right. Can I reply now?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: There's a mistake, if the interpreter can interpret this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said no?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: It says here yes. I didn't say "yes," I said "no."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We see the correction that you have made. We note it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you explain to Their Honours what Sarajevo means to you, I mean in terms of territory. Where is Sarajevo, on what territory?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: In my view, Sarajevo is the biggest city, the capital city, in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and there are three rivers, Zeljeznica, the Miljacka, and the Bosna running through it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where these three rivers flow?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: The Miljacka goes from Pale towards Bascarsija, Drvenija, Stari Grad, through Grbavica, Potoke, Alipasino Polje, and it flows into the river Bosna near Stup near Ilidza. The Miljacka -- or rather the Zeljeznica has its source in Trnovo. It passes through Trnovo, below Ceskavica [phoen] through Kijevo, Krupac, Lojkovici [as interpreted], Sokolovic Kolonija, and at Ilidza at a place called Sustavci it flows into the Bosna and those two rivers together make up the river Bosna which flows through a part of Ilidza, Vogosca, and Ilijas, and then it flows on towards Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us the Zeljeznica flows by the airport, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: It's near the new airport at a distance of about a thousand metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And the place through which the Zeljaznica flows, what is its name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Well, it's a large part of Vojkovici, then Sokolovic Kolonija, it's near Hrasnica and Butmir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to Their Honours around those three rivers, the Miljacka, the Zeljeznica, and the Bosna, what is the configuration of the terrain like? What hills are there around those three rivers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Overlooking those three rivers are Mojmilo, Stupsko Brdo, Zuc, Sokolje, Hum, Grdonj, Trebevic, and around Trebevic, at its foot-hills are Colina Kapa, Debelo Brdo and Vidikovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware of when General Dragomir Milosevic arrived at the head of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Dragomir Milosevic arrived in early August 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now tell me one more thing before I move on. The area around those three rivers and the hills surrounding those three rivers, what did this look like in relation to what was called Sarajevo? What was Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Those hills that dominated over the town of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that was not what I was asking you, but let's not make things complicated. At the point in time when Mr. Dragomir Milosevic took over command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, who had control of the hills you have just mentioned, saying they were around those three rivers, in that area?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: The hills were held by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Mojmilo was under the control of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Sokolje was also, as was Zuc, Hum, and Grdonj.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And on the south-eastern side?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: At Trebevic, Colina Kapa, and Debelo Brdo were under the control of the BH army, whereas Vidikovac and part of Zlatiste were under the control of the army of Republika Srpska -- and that was where the road passed through linking us up to Pale and the rest of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to ask you a question. When you say that the hills were held by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, exactly what do you mean? Do you mean the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina alone occupied the hills or that they occupied a particular section which gave them a dominant view? Were there other forces on those hills, apart from the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I can say is that they held those hills and dominated on those hills, as I have just said, at Mojmilo, at Hum, at Grdonj, at Zuc, at Sokolje, at Colina Kapa, at Debelo Brdo beneath Trebevic, whereas the Serb army was at Zlatiste and Vidikovac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trapara, tell me now, when Dragomir Milosevic took up command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, which army did you belong to and where were you at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: I belonged to the Army of Republika Srpska. I was a member of the 1st Sarajevo Brigade, the 1st Battalion, 1st Company, 1st Platoon, in Dobrinja I, Dobrinja IV, towards Donji Kotorac between the new airport and the old airport in the direction of Hrasnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now show you a map of Sarajevo, this is 65 ter 2872.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in on the southern part, the south-western part of the map? Can we scroll up a bit? A little to the west, please, so that we can see the airport, to the west. More. More. More to the south, more to the south -- ah, yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you indicate approximately where you lived before you went to Donji Kotorac.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: You mean where my house was?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, when you were still working in Famos, can you mark it.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Just a moment, can I just see where Famos is here. You can't see Hrasnica here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, just mark the place where you were in your family house during the conflict. Show us where Donji Kotorac is.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Just slowly, please. Take it easy. And make a circle where your house was.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Here, around here. Maybe a bit further up. Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Please mark it with a K.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And now draw the separation line between the Army of Republika Srpska and the 1st Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where was -- or rather, do you know what there was below the airport?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: There was a tunnel underneath the airport, through which the Army of BH passed and their civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you show how far the exit from the tunnel was in relation to your house?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Well, it was some 500 metres away from my house, but in relation to the front line it was about 200 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark on the map where approximately this was?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: If you can --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: I'll mark it with a T for tunnel --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but make a circle here.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You just said that General Dragomir Milosevic became the commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. What was the situation at the time when he arrived in early August?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Well, in early August 1994, there was a relative lull, a calm, and the Muslim forces made use of this to go through the tunnel, to go towards Treskavica and Igman.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: As you said, the exit from the tunnel was 200 metres away. Who else passed by, apart from the soldiers?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Apart from the soldiers, the BH army, there were also civilians, the civilian population passing through the tunnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: As you said, from the separation line where you were, it was 200 metres away. And you said that both soldiers and civilians passed by. Did you fire from your positions towards those people with any kind of weapon?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: No, we did not. We did not, because it was not our aim to provoke a lot of fighting down there because our own civilian population lived there, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was there any significance in the fact that soldiers and civilians passed through together?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Yes, there was. The army made use of that in order to pass through as safely as possible and take up positions on the surrounding hills. I forgot to say that there was a mountain overlooking this area, the mountain of Igman.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Donji Kotorac is a place you mentioned. Can you show where the hill of Mojmilo is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it says Mojmilo here, but where is the hill, actually, the highest elevation of Mojmilo? Over which area does Mojmilo extend? Can you indicate that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Well, from Nedzarici --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, draw that, draw that.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Like this over -- all of this was Mojmilo.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mark this with an M.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And over here, towards the south and the south-west, what was the situation? What hills were there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You just mentioned Igman.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Yes, Igman. The dominating feature was Mount Igman. There's also Crni Vrh, Debelo Brdo, Tresnjevo Brdo, and from Mount Igman you can see the entire city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the event we might be continuing along this topic in the examination-in-chief, I feel I need to say so far this whole story of who dominated what hills around Sarajevo wasn't even mentioned in the 65 ter summary that we received. And I've been giving this some leeway, but at this point, Your Honour, I have to say when the Prosecution knows in advance that there will be witnesses talking about the elevations around the city and who held of them, we have maps, we have photographs and diagrams that we've typically been able to use to prepare these witnesses and use in their examination-in-chief. And if I had known that there was going to be extensive testimony about the hills, the elevations, and control of them, I would have prepared accordingly. However, that's not the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I hear the submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in French before me, I have it here. In one place it says: [In French] "The army around Hrasnica and Gornji Kotorac. The formation of military units and the confrontation line between the two factions, the two warring factions" -- [in B/C/S] and so on and so forth. Therefore, we have the places specified. We know where this gentleman's position was and everything else pertaining to the conflict of the two warring parties. I was following this. We've come up to his positions. He was explaining to us what Sarajevo was and who was at which positions, because he was a combatant of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. He is familiar with all of these things. Therefore --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I don't see what it is that we should have included.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned three elevations on Igman. I cannot recall exactly which hills those were, but what was their altitude, approximately?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Over 1.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Then I have to ask you to indicate those elevations on the map. Please get up and do not reply but merely try to locate them on the map. Please have a look at what the exact altitude of those elevations is. What is the altitude?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What did you say, what was your position in relation to that, and not only your positions but everything that was below those elevations?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: The situation was such that the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had full control over our positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said that initially there was a lull. When did problems begin?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Gradually. The Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina used the tunnel to move, to go via Igman and to regroup at Treskavica as well as other parts of the theatre. They used that time to carry out sabotage actions in order to try and push the Serb lines back. In September and October 1994 in one such sabotage attack in the area of Treskavica, I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, is it time for a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we have another minute and a half, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me this: How many troops left Sarajevo? How many troops moved through the tunnel and onwards towards the positions you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: It is difficult to say, but there were troops and civilians non-stop, around-the-clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What was happening at Hrasnica? How far is Hrasnica from your positions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Hrasnica is such -- well, the closest point of it was towards Famos and towards Ilidza, the distance may have been some 3 or 400 metres. The centre of Hrasnica, where the command was and the rest, well it's up to 1 kilometre away.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Who held Famos, the factory you used to work in?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Famos, as such, was partially in the hands of the Army of Republika Srpska, whereas the other part was in the hands of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, we'll take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton -- ah, it's Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: While we're still on the map, and so as not to have to go back to it later, since I want to move on to some other documents, I wanted to do something else. You've marked Mojmilo and you've marked the separation line. Can you mark the road which led from Donji Kotorac to Zlatiste, mark it there, please, across the map, wherever you see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: I don't see the foundation here that might go to support the witness's ability to identify a road. In fact, I'm still uncertain as to what the witness might have been doing over the course of the period of the indictment to be able to base any of his -- or to found any of the observations he's making.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, establish a foundation for the witness's ability to give this evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By putting questions, you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you belong to the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What were you in that army?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: A soldier and a platoon commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Were you able to use or were you expected to use the roads in order to carry out your activities in relation to your permanent positions at Gornji Kotorac?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: No, Donji Kotorac.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Donji Kotorac.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Yes, I did, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Did you also go to Zlatiste in the period relevant for the indictment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Yes, I did, to Zlatiste, it was the only way to move from Donji Kotorac to Pale and other parts of Republika Srpska --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's sufficient. Move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To go back to the first thing I wanted to ask the witness. I wanted to ask him to mark the road he had to use if he was supposed to carry out a certain task. Where was he supposed to go, for example, if he wanted to go to Pale.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Up here, Lukavica, and on to Pale. It's difficult to get my bearings on this map since things are a bit unclear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In relation to Mojmilo, what was the position of the road?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: A part of that road went just below Mojmilo at the foot.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What was happening while you were passing by Mojmilo?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: During combat activities, that part of the road was exposed to firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to the time for which General Milosevic was charged with. You said that there was a lull at that time. Where were combat operations carried out at that time? You've already told us you were wounded.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: I was waiting for the transcript to stop. At that time there were activities in the area of Treskavica, Nisic, and the surrounding hills.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What was happening around Famos, where the factory was in which you used to work during the time of command of Dragomir Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: That was the front line. It even went through the Famos facility, and a part of the factory was used for some sort of production at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At that time, on those positions where you were, were there any heavy pieces there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: No. At that time all of the heavy pieces had already been pulled out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Please, finish your answer.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: There were no heavy pieces there at the time. By that time it had been pulled out beyond its range limit. I don't know exactly how far.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Hrasnica and Igman, you mentioned the altitudes. Did they fire upon you from those areas and by using what weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You already explained that Igman was above Hrasnica, the elevations that were there. Was there any firing from there?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: At one point they fired from Igman with their artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I was actually thinking about the time that you mentioned, October when you were wounded.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Yes, but that was at Treskavica. At the time they used the regrouping of their army and occasionally they managed to attack positions of the Army of Republika Srpska. In that period when I was wounded, there was a relative truce. We were at our positions. We were leaving to go home, and their sabotage group conducted an attack. They intercepted a truck, and some 13 to 15 people were killed or wounded there. That's when I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And when did things quieten down?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Shortly after that there was a relative truce, and this went on like that until June, until the summer, early summer of 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And when did the first skirmishes begin, what was May like?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: May was the month of truce. I think that the blue road also went through that section, but during the truce on the 12th of May, 1995, they managed to hit my [Realtime transcript read in error "by"] mother and another woman who were working in the fields. At the time they were just resting in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What happened after that? And what was your mother's name and what was the other woman?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: My mother is Mara Trapara and the other woman was called Vera Novakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened later in May and onwards?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: After that, there was the regrouping. They started to go through the tunnel, to the neighbouring mountains, and they were preparing for a frontal attack on all Serb positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before I continue to examine this witness, could we please save this map and I would like it to be tendered as a Defence exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D274, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 32, line 22, instead of "by" it says "may."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Page 32, line -- managed to hit my mother, and we have "by." Well, we thank you for that correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And this map, has it now been admitted? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, can you please explain, you said that until May it was quiet. Can you describe that time until May when you say that it was quiet, at your positions primarily.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: It was quiet. We carried out our regular assignments. Their army was passing through the tunnel day and night, we knew that, we observed it, but we didn't react to it because it wasn't our objective to provoke actions. Families lived along those lines, the family Novakovic lived along those lines. A man was killed along that line also by a sniper. I forgot to mention that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: In front of you was Hrasnica. Did you ever hear of anyone getting killed from the snipers on the other side, from these positions where you were?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: No, never, I never heard of anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: During that time of truce, the B&H army was constantly going through the tunnel and it was at a distance of some 200 metres from you. Does this document accord with what you are saying? I'm going to show you document DD002665. Document DD002665. Mr. Trapara, can you please look at the heading of the document, the date, and what it says below, and then can you read these first sections. And then after that I can put questions to you after the explanations that you have provided.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Division command, strictly confidential, 02/2-2-153, rotation of the 12th KoV and division of the 16th land army, zone of responsibility order. "In order to carry out the routine rotation of the 12th KoVd unit the battalion commands resubordinated to the 16th KoVd, and undertake all the necessary measures for unit preparation and organisation for the rotation, I issue the following order. "Brigade commands shall immediately undertake all the necessary measures to prepare the units - battalions for rotation of the 16th Division's area of responsibility. "During the preparations of the battalions for rotation observe all current orders related to the numbers of officers and soldiers who are dispatched to carry out combat actions."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you. The document of the 6th of August, 1995, actually speaks about what you have already testified about, that you watched them going out of the tunnel and going to their positions. So this was on the 6th of August, 1995. How long did you have the opportunity to monitor this? This is the 6th of August, 1995. How long before this did you notice that and what was the intensity of this occurrence in this particular period?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: You mean the passage through the tunnel. They were constantly going through the tunnel throughout 1994 and 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Even in this quiet period when you were not undertaking any actions, as you say?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Yes, all the time, even in the quiet times.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please tender this exhibit as -- this document as a Defence exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As D275, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trapara, could you please tell me now what happened. You already described what was going on in May and what happened to your mother. And what happened then, in May and in subsequent months that followed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: In this period when this document - because this is on the 6th of August - then the Muslim army prepared a large action throughout the whole territory of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. The document is of the 6th of August, but when did this begin?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: I didn't understand. What?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said May, the document is of the 6th of August. Please listen to me. When did that offensive that you're talking about begin?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: I don't know when it began. I know it was summer, June, July, August, I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And how did it look like?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: First, they struck the frontal positions. As far as my area of responsibility is concerned, they struck Dobrinja I and Dobrinja IV and the town area in the direction of Zlatiste. They were hitting our forces and then they wanted to approach from the back of the front, Treskavica, Nisici, Treskavica, and other positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to show you document D107, that's been a Defence exhibit for a long time now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So can we now look at that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trapara, can you please, very slowly, because we will finish with this examination-in-chief quickly. Can you very slowly read the heading, the date, and what it says below the heading, and in particular this first paragraph and then I would like to ask you something.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: "Command of the 12th division, strictly confidential, number 02/2-7-10 -- command of the 12th division, strictly confidential, number 02/2-7-10, Sarajevo, the 26th of June, 1995. "Defence of the republic, military secret, strictly confidential, 1. "Proposal of targets chosen for destruction and tying up the aggressor forces by units. "To the commander of the 1st Corps. "Pursuant to the order of the 1st Corps Chief of Staff, strictly confidential number 01/3-151 dated the 25th of June, 1995, to execute active combat operations in the area of responsibility of all brigades in the area of responsibility of the 12th Army Division in order to tie up the aggressor forces around the city and to stretch out the same offering relief to our forces outside the city zone in the area of the responsibility of the 14th and the 16th Army Division we send you proposals brigade by brigade."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this what you said before about what these activities looked like of the 1st Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina when you were talking about focusing on specific actions. Can you explain that again, the way you did a little bit before, now after you have read this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This was all with the objective of tying the units of the Army of Republika Srpska to specific positions, and for them to be able to use other positions to created confusion and a breakthrough.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what is being said in this first paragraph here, that talks about the 101st Brigade, and then -- can you read that. And then at the very end can you please read another paragraph and then I will put some questions to you after that. Can you please read the part that relates to the 101st Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: "The 101st Mountain Brigade. "The 1st Mountain Brigade in the area of responsibility. "The bunker and access from the road to the tunnel Dzakina Kuca gun holes from the eastern and western sides. "The hand-held launcher, anti-tank grenade launcher, squad and sniper rifle and automatic rifle."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the end of the document now, that is page 2 in B/C/S and it's the end of the document in English. It's the third page, not the second page, please, excuse me, the third page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: The end of that page where it says under 3 bb, can you please read all of that until the end.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: "Objective 1: MG in the D. Ponjarca Street first floor Dobrinja IV group aim the RPG and the commander, the assistant marksman, the sniper, and two automatic rifle operators, approves the expenditure of two RPG projectiles, one combat kit for the PASP. 0.5 combat kit for automatic rifle, target 2, the dormitory in the Miroslava Krleze Street Dobrinja I group, marksman, RPG commander, at the same time, assistant marksman, sniper operator, and two automatic weapons operators. Approve the expenditure of two RPG projectiles, one combat kit for the PASP and one combat kit for the AP."

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you now look at the last page and tell us who signed that as an order.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Commander brigadier Fikret Prevljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now since you've already said what you said about the beginning section of this document and these two combat assignments that were issued, what do you know -- you already said the date and it was all the way it is described here. What do you know in relation to where this was in relation to your positions and what do you know about these two actions?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: I can tell you specifically about these two actions because they happened in the area of responsibility of my battalion and my company. It happened in the D. Ponjarca and Miroslava Krleze in Dobrinja I and Dobrinja IV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. With respect to the portion the witness just read out he's read that out, Your Honours, because that portion hasn't been translated into English, and now the witness is leading evidence about information which is new to the English speakers of this Trial Chamber which was not in the least disclosed to the Prosecution prior to his testifying. So I would object on both of those grounds. I've had no notice whatsoever, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So what you are saying is that the piece that he read out beginning at -- where is it? 30 -- it's on the transcript but that piece was not translated?

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: As far as I can see, and I've been trying to find that portion on the English document available to us on e-court. It was not translated at all. So for the witness to go further, Your Honour, I would suggest would be inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I would agree, Mr. Tapuskovic. Why wasn't it translated?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This entire document has been translated. I didn't pay attention to the English, but it has been translated. Everything I have read out has been translated into English, and it was disclosed on time. The entire document was translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you have anything to confirm that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It can be brought up, Your Honours. Let us see the first page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We're not talking about the document as a whole but the particular piece that Ms. Edgerton has highlighted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But everything has been translated. If we can first see the first page referring to the action of the 101st Brigade. It begins on page 1, and that last event is on the last page, and it's all been translated, 3 bb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton, is the passage beginning 3 -- the 3 -- the 3rd bb, the sleeping quarters, is that the one to which you referred? Because it's in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Yes, now I see it, Your Honours, and I was struggling to find it as the witness was giving his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Tapuskovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Trapara, these two events described here which occurred, as you have already said, in your area of responsibility. What can you say about them? Do you have any direct knowledge of this, of the way events unfolded?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: As for these two events, I can say -- well, I don't know if it was exactly on that day, but it was at that time. They attacked the entire part of Serb territory from Zlatiste and Debelo Brdo all the way to Dobrinja I and the airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And as you were there holding those positions, Dzakina Kuca is mentioned and then Ponjarca, D. Ponjarca. In view of this location, what do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Dobrinja Ponjarca Street was in Dobrinja IV and Dzakina Kuca is a house on the other side of the airport towards the front held by the Ilidza Brigade. They -- and also Dobrinja I at the same time. So they launched their assault on these points in order to stretch out the forces of Republika Srpska and to be able to go towards Treskavica, Hadzica, and those parts where there was a war theatre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: This other event that has to do with Miraslova Krleze Street, Dobrinja IV and Dobrinja I, did it distract your attention? That's what I wanted to ask you.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Well, as my company was linked to Dobrinja I, that was our area of responsibility. We sent some of our troops to help there. An entire platoon had to go and help in order to prevent them breaking through because they had broken through at Trebevic in that time-period when they managed to pierce through the Serb lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And where was this?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: Well, I don't know precisely but there was a part of Debelo Brdo and Zlatiste around Vidikovac, that part up there, I don't know exactly what part. And so we had to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand the entire reply, response, the last part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Would you just repeat the last thing you said, Mr. Witness, your last sentence, the interpreter did not get it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I? In order to secure ourselves and make sure that the Muslim forces must not break through our lines, we had to strengthen our lines. Dobrinja I and Dobrinja IV, we had a lot of our own civilian population. I didn't say that just a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And tell me, what exactly did you find out happened at Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: At the same time they managed to break through some lines at Trebevic, some lines of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: What did this look like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, given that Trebevic is so far outside of the confrontation lines with which we're concerned in these proceedings, I wonder -- I don't see any foundation for the witness's knowledge as regard to what happened at Trebevic which I don't think, with respect, is within the area of responsibility of his brigade. So perhaps that foundation could be established.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. -- Sorry, Ms. Edgerton, I don't agree with you. If you wish, you can take it up in cross-examination and test his knowledge, but he's a soldier in the army and I take it that he has familiarity with these areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, to clarify this, you said what you did, but how do you know about the events at Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
utterances.text: All of this was in the area of responsibility of my brigade, this was the 1st Sarajevo Brigade. Our area of responsibility was from the river Zeljeznica all the way up to Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have already ruled. Just proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, to round off this topic, in peacetime, the area across Zlatiste, were there some actions threatening the area at Zlatiste from the area under the control of the 1st Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Not in peacetime but when there was a lull in the fighting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A part of the road leading from Sarajevo across Zlatiste towards Pale was under fire from the Muslim forces day and night. Trucks and buses passed by and luxury cars, and there were a lot of casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell us, you lived in Hrasnica while you were still able to work in Famos. What happened in 1992 that made you leave your job and the house in which you had lived, your home, in order to go to Kotorac?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Edgerton.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're two years outside of the indictment period here. I would object on the ground of relevance. We're temporally outside of the relevant period for this indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. How do you respond to that, Mr. Tapuskovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, at this point I don't think I have to deal with that extensively, but the time-period from 1992 is in the indictment. It deals with that period. It is in the indictment, and I simply cannot believe that this is constantly being raised as an issue. But in order to save time, I don't think it's that important for this witness to deal with that. But it is important to deal with the time preceding General Dragomir Milosevic's time. So I have to repeat at this point that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, I've said before that the mere fact that the indictment period starts in 1994, but one is able to refer to the pre-indictment period, 1992, because that is also covered in the indictment, that doesn't mean that any and every piece of evidence relating to 1992 or 1993 will be admitted. You still have to justify the relevance of the evidence. That's the first basis for admissibility: Relevance. So merely to say it is 1992 will not let the evidence in, you know. But I see you are not insisting on it, so let us proceed to another point.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Why did you take up weapons in 1992, in view of the place where you lived and the job you did --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. -- If you are going to lead evidence about 1992, it must be evidence that is relevant to the indictment. Is the evidence that you propose to lead now relevant?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I started questioning the witness from paragraph 6, and the witness gave us some very valid evidence about paragraph 6, what Sarajevo is, that it's surrounded by hills and slopes, steep slopes. He explained what this is and who held those mountains, and then in points 7 and 8: "In Sarajevo armed hostilities broke out soon after on the 7th of April, 1992, Bosnia-Herzegovina," and so on and so forth. So the circumstances in which armed hostilities broke out and when I could continue from point to point, from paragraph to paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tapuskovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- I didn't want to dwell on it long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, if you can, explain as briefly as possible what prompted you and the people around you to take up weapons and to leave your homes and your jobs and to go to your family house?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN TRAPARA
